h1: The 7 Best Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 leaf blowers across gas backpack, gas handheld and cordless battery, compared on listed CFM, format and price tier.
summary: The Milwaukee M18 FUEL is the best leaf blower for most homes: 450 CFM, 120 MPH and no fuel to mix. If you want more air from a battery, the DEWALT 60V MAX lists 600 CFM. Big properties are better served by a gas backpack, with the Husqvarna 150BT for value and the Echo X Series for maximum airflow. The MZK is the budget gamble.
intro: Ask ten people which leaf blower to buy and you will hear ten brand names. The better question is which kind. A gas backpack and an 18 volt handheld are built for different jobs, and buying the wrong format is the most expensive mistake in this category. People with a quarter acre end up hauling 80cc engines they hate starting, while owners of wooded lots buy compact battery units that run flat halfway through the front yard.

This ranking crosses formats on purpose. We reviewed seven blowers, battery handhelds and gas backpacks alike, and scored them on the Primea framework. Listed airflow mattered most, but we also weighed power source, upkeep, platform cost and how well each machine matches the yard it is realistically bought for.

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL 120 MPH 450 CFM 18-Volt Lithium Ion Brushless Blower
products.verdict: Strong airflow with no gas to mix.
products.description:
Milwaukee's M18 FUEL handheld is the blower we would hand to most homeowners. Its brushless 18 volt motor is rated at 450 CFM and 120 MPH, and it sells in the $100 to $200 tier. There is no fuel to mix and no pull cord to fight.

It takes first place because it hits the point where most suburban yards are fully covered without the noise and upkeep of gas. The DEWALT 60V moves more air, but needs a heavier, pricier battery system. The gas backpacks below move far more, but they are overkill for a typical lot.

Buy it if you already own M18 tools or have an average yard with some trees. The honest caveat is runtime: one battery may not finish a heavily wooded property, so a second pack is worth budgeting for.

products.name: DEWALT 60V MAX Axial Handheld Blower DCBL772B
products.description:
The DEWALT DCBL772B is the strongest battery blower in this ranking. Its 60V MAX axial fan is rated at 600 CFM in a handheld body, and it sells in the $100 to $200 tier. That is a third more listed airflow than the Milwaukee above it.

So why second? Because the 60V platform is a separate ecosystem from DEWALT's common 20V line. If you do not already own 60V batteries, the real cost climbs once you add a pack and charger. The Milwaukee fits more existing tool collections and covers most yards with less spend.

Buy it if you want the most cordless airflow here, already own DEWALT 60V gear, or have a larger yard but want to avoid gas. Skip it if you are buying into a battery platform from scratch.

products.name: Husqvarna 150BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.description:
The Husqvarna 150BT is our pick for anyone who has outgrown battery power. It lists 765 CFM from a gas backpack and lands in the $200 to $500 tier. That is far more air than any handheld here, with the weight carried on your shoulders.

It ranks third because gas brings real costs in fuel, mixing, maintenance and noise that most homeowners do not need to take on. Against the Echo X Series below it, though, it is the better value: substantial airflow from a well-supported brand at well under the Echo's price.

Buy it for a large lot, long sessions or heavy autumn leaf fall. Skip it if you live under strict noise rules or simply do not want to store gasoline, because battery blowers above it are far easier to live with.

products.name: Echo 220 MPH 1110 CFM 79.9 cc Gas 2-Stroke X Series Backpack Blower
products.verdict: 1110 CFM for acreage and pro work.
products.description:
Echo's X Series backpack is the most powerful machine we ranked, by some distance. A 79.9cc two-stroke engine pushes a listed 1110 CFM at 220 MPH, and it sits in the $500+ tier.

It ranks fourth, not first, because that power has a narrow audience. Most homes simply do not need 1110 CFM, and paying the top tier for it, plus fuel, weight and noise, makes little sense on a normal lot. For acreage and landscaping work, though, it is the blower everything else is measured against.

Buy it if you clear acres, run a landscaping business or face deep, wet autumn drifts every year. For anything smaller, the Husqvarna 150BT gives you serious gas airflow for far less money and less weight on your back.

products.name: Husqvarna 125B Gas Leaf Blower
products.description:
The Husqvarna 125B is a gas handheld rated at 470 CFM. It lives in the $200 to $500 tier, above the price of the Milwaukee battery blower.

That comparison is the whole story behind its rank. The Milwaukee lists nearly the same airflow, costs less, needs no fuel and starts with a trigger. The 125B makes sense in one situation: you already keep two-stroke fuel for a chainsaw or trimmer and want unlimited runtime without charging batteries between sessions.

Buy it if you prefer gas, need to work for long stretches without stopping, or live where cold weather saps battery performance. Skip it if you are starting fresh, because a battery handheld does the same job with far less upkeep.

products.name: MZK 20V Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 450 CFM in the lowest price tier.
products.description:
The MZK is the budget wildcard. It lists 450 CFM on a 20V battery, the same headline airflow as the Milwaukee, and sits in the $25 to $50 tier, a fraction of the price of anything above it.

It ranks sixth because a listing claim and a proven tool are different things. MZK has no track record we can lean on, the battery is not part of any major tool platform, and replacement packs or parts may be hard to find in a couple of years. That leaves it behind every name brand here on build confidence and long-term value.

Buy it if you have a small yard, a patio or a driveway to clear a few times a year and want the cheapest cordless option. Skip it if you expect the blower to last many seasons.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Blower
products.verdict: A compact 100 CFM blower for light clean-up.
products.description:
DEWALT's 20V MAX blower is a compact clean-up tool, not a leaf mover. It lists 100 CFM in a cordless body and sits in the $100 to $200 tier. It runs on the same 20V batteries many people already own for drills and drivers.

It ranks last because 100 CFM is a small fraction of what the other blowers here deliver. That is far too little for a lawn full of leaves. What it does well is quick work: grass clippings on a path, sawdust in a garage, a dusty deck after a storm.

Buy it if you already own DEWALT 20V batteries and want a light tool for hard surfaces. For actual leaf clearing, step up to the Milwaukee M18 FUEL or the DEWALT 60V model above.

methodology.title: Format fit
methodology.description: Backpack, handheld and cordless were judged on the yards they suit.

methodology.title: Power source
methodology.description: Gas and battery tradeoffs were weighed.

whatMatters.detail: CFM measures how much air the blower moves each minute, and it is the single best indicator of how quickly leaves will clear. Compare like with like: a 450 CFM handheld is strong, while backpacks start much higher. Find the figure in the title or spec table. If a cheap blower claims flagship airflow, as the MZK does, treat the number with caution.

Gas offers unlimited runtime and the highest airflow, but needs fuel mixing, regular maintenance and tolerance for noise. Battery blowers start instantly, need almost no upkeep and run quieter, but stop when the pack is empty. For most yards under half an acre, battery is the better fit. Check the power source in the title and whether a battery is included.

Handheld blowers are lighter to grab and store, but the full weight hangs from one arm. Backpacks shift the load to your shoulders and hips, which is what lets the Husqvarna 150BT or Echo X Series run for an hour comfortably. Match the format to your typical session length. If clearing takes more than 30 minutes, a backpack earns its place.

MPH is the speed of the air leaving the nozzle. High speed lifts wet, matted leaves and debris wedged into gravel or mulch, which volume alone pushes past. Ideally a listing gives both figures. The Milwaukee lists 120 MPH and the Echo X Series 220 MPH. A spec sheet that only advertises speed is often hiding a low CFM figure.

For battery blowers, the platform matters as much as the tool. Batteries are the expensive part, so staying with one system across your mower, trimmer and drill saves real money. For gas, a local dealer network makes servicing simple. Check which battery the blower takes, whether it is included, and where the nearest authorized service center is.

faq.a: Battery for most homes. A blower like the Milwaukee M18 FUEL covers a typical suburban lot with no fuel, little maintenance and less noise. Gas, like the Husqvarna 150BT, earns its keep on large or wooded properties where you need long sessions and more airflow.

Buying too much blower. A gas backpack like the Echo X Series is a wonderful machine for acreage, but on a small lot it is heavy, loud and fussy to maintain. Size the blower to your yard, then pick the brand.

If you already own DEWALT 60V batteries or have a large yard and refuse to go gas, yes. It lists 600 CFM, a third more than the Milwaukee. If you are buying the platform from scratch, the Milwaukee M18 FUEL is better value.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Battery blowers like the Milwaukee and DEWALT need only a charged pack and the nozzle clicked on. Gas models like the Husqvarna 150BT need fuel mixed at the ratio in the manual, a few primer presses and an adjusted harness before the first start.

Keep the air intake clear of leaves and debris every time you use it. For gas models, use fresh fuel, clean the air filter each season and run the tank dry before storage. Battery packs last longest stored partly charged in a cool, dry place.

They are generally much quieter than gas, especially at lower speed settings, though no blower is silent. In noise-restricted neighborhoods a battery model like the Milwaukee M18 FUEL or DEWALT 60V is usually the safer choice than any two-stroke backpack.

finalTake: For most homes, the Milwaukee M18 FUEL is the right leaf blower: strong airflow, no gas and minimal upkeep. If you want more battery power, the DEWALT 60V is the step up. Large properties belong to gas, with the Husqvarna 150BT for value and the Echo X Series when nothing less than maximum airflow will do. Size the blower to the yard first, and the choice gets easy.
